capabilities: Validate and import Daily, Weekly, Budget, and Medical Markdown forms into a vault-local SQLite database
Display calendar and dashboards for time, finances, nutrition, exercise, engagements, and health records
Manage canonical catalogs of engagements, foods, accounts, exercises, medications, and aliases
Stage catalog changes and transactions into unimported Daily Forms for review before confirming
Create database backups and support full-day reimport with an explicit replacement warning
extras: Stores all records in a SQLite .db file inside the vault rather than in notes; the README recommends independent vault backups before upgrades and says each vault represents one owner, so other people's records need separate vaults. The README is the full user manual; developer docs and changelog live in DEVELOPMENT.md and CHANGELOG.md.
intentEvidence: This project began as a fork of seonggoos/obsidian-schedule-calendar.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to turn journal notes into validated structured records with reviewable dashboards for time, finances, nutrition, exercise, and medical history.

relations.evidence: This project began as a fork of seonggoos/obsidian-schedule-calendar.

summary: Life-tracking system that validates Markdown forms, imports them into a vault-local SQLite database, and shows calendar and dashboards for time, money, food, exercise, and health.
